items.title: Lay out error reports in one private package

goal.title: Lay out error reports in one private package
criteria: There is one place that decides a report's wording, and the existing report output is unchanged
Detail can be wrapped at any width, or left whole when the width is 0
Every problem inside an error is found, including through application wrapping and joined errors, without descending into a problem's own cause

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: The wording now lives only in internal/report/report.go Layout (lines 105-156): the "Error"/"Warning" labels, ": "+summary, the "  on <file> line N, in E, field F:" location, the "(source code not available)" line, the gutter format "  %4d | " and the blank-line endings. diagnostics.go:31-38 only calls report.Layout and labels the segments, with no wording of its own. Comparing the removed code in xcl.diff (lines 78-124 and 126-163) with Layout, each string and newline matches, so the output appears unchanged. I did not run the tests, so this rests on reading the code.

internal/report/wrap.go:7-12: Wrap returns detail unchanged when width <= 0, and otherwise calls wordwrap.WrapString(detail, uint(width)). diagnostics.go:106-107 applies it to the Detail segment only, so source lines are never wrapped.

internal/report/walk.go:10-33: Walk calls visit and returns as soon as isProblem(err) is true, so a problem's Cause is never visited. For other errors it descends through both Unwrap() []error (joined errors) and Unwrap() error (application wrapping), but only when Contains reports a problem beneath them (walk.go:37-58). Contains also checks Unwrap() []error before Unwrap() error. Note: nothing outside the report package calls Walk yet (grep found only walk_test.go), so the errors package does not use it in this diff. The criterion is judged on the function's behaviour, which the code shows.

items.title: Capture two lines of context around each fault

goal.title: Capture two lines of context around each fault
criteria: A fault in the middle of a file captures the two lines before and the two after it
A fault on line 1 of a three-line file captures lines 1 to 3
A fault on the last line captures that line and the two before it
No file is read again to capture context

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: errors/diagnostic.go:123-124 sets start = max(1, first-contextLines) and end = max(last, min(lineCount, last+contextLines)) with contextLines = 2 (line 136). errors/diagnostic_test.go TestNewDiagnosticInTheMiddleOfAFileTakesTwoLinesEitherSide (diff lines 409-413) puts a fault on line 5 of the nine-line longSource and expects Start 3 and lines 3 to 7, which the code produces.

errors/diagnostic.go:123-124: for a fault on line 1 of the three-line source, start = max(1, -1) = 1 and lineCount = 3 (the trailing empty element from the final newline is dropped at lines 118-121), so end = 3. errors/diagnostic_test.go TestNewDiagnosticOnTheFirstLineOfAThreeLineFileTakesLinesOneToThree (diff lines 416-421) expects Start 1 and lines 1 to 3.

errors/diagnostic.go:123-124: for a fault on line 9 of the nine-line longSource, start = 7 and end = max(9, min(9, 11)) = 9, so lines 7 to 9 are taken and the empty trailing element is excluded. errors/diagnostic_test.go TestNewDiagnosticOnTheLastLineTakesThatLineAndTheTwoBefore (diff lines 423-428) expects Start 7 and lines name, enabled and closing brace.

No os.ReadFile or os.Open exists in errors/ (grep found none). linesOf (errors/diagnostic.go:97-132) slices the src bytes passed in by the caller, so context comes from memory. The only read is internal/parser/parser.go:817 in parseFile, which reads each file once per parse and stores the bytes at line 831; the diff does not add a read. errors/diagnostic_test.go TestNewDiagnosticNeverReadsTheFileForContext (diff lines 464-473) backs this by writing the file, passing a different in-memory source, and expecting the context from the in-memory bytes.

items.title: Print the full report through detailed error formatting

goal.title: Print the full report through detailed error formatting
criteria: Formatting a configuration error in its ordinary form gives a single line
Asking for its detailed form gives the full report with the surrounding lines, detail wrapped at 80 columns
Logging the error with zap writes the full plain report in the entry's detailed error field
zap is used only by tests, at a pinned version

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: errors/format.go:25-27 and 39-41 route %v and %s on *Diagnostic and *ConfigError to formatError, which writes err.Error() (format.go:53-56). errors/format_test.go:33-43 checks %v and %s equal the one-line Error(). format_test.go:111-116 (TestConfigErrorWithOneProblemFormattedWithVIsASingleLine) checks a single problem's %v contains no newline.

errors/format.go:46-62 and 68-89: %+v on the error calls plainReport, which lays out the report from report.Layout and wraps the Detail segment with report.Wrap at reportWidth = 80 (format.go:14, 80). internal/report/wrap.go:7-12 wraps with go-wordwrap at the given width. format_test.go:51-53 checks the full expected report, including the numbered context lines 1-3 around the fault. format_test.go:97-109 checks every wrapped detail line is <= 80 columns and that the detail spans more than one line.

errors/format_zap_test.go:19-35 builds a *ConfigError holding a Diagnostic with source. Lines 37-53 log it with zap.Error through a zapcore JSON encoder and unmarshal the entry. Lines 55-62 (TestZapLogsTheReportOfAConfigErrorInErrorVerbose) require entry["errorVerbose"] to equal fmt.Sprintf("%+v", ce) and to contain the numbered gutter line. Lines 64-70 check the error field is the one-line message. The mechanism is format.go:39-41, which implements fmt.Formatter on *ConfigError. Note: the test covers a ConfigError passed directly, not one wrapped by another error; format.go:21-24 and 35-38 document that %+v does not apply to wrapping errors.

go.mod:23 requires go.uber.org/zap v1.27.0 with the comment 'test only: errors/format_zap_test.go proves zap.Error logs the report in errorVerbose'; it is pinned to an exact version. go.sum:504-505 has the matching hashes, and go.sum:519-524 adds goleak and multierr. A grep of the code root for 'go.uber.org/zap' and 'zap.' finds imports only in errors/format_zap_test.go:10-11, which is a _test.go file in package errors_test. No non-test .go file imports zap (the other matches are unrelated 'zap' function names in internal/xcl/hclsyntax test fixtures, or prose in .spektacular docs). Caveat: go.mod places zap in the direct require block, not marked // indirect, which is consistent with a direct test import. The one-line comment in go.mod is the only in-file statement that it is test-only.

items.title: Rebuild highlighting around kinds, themes and formatters

goal.title: Rebuild highlighting around kinds, themes and formatters
criteria: Configuration text is labelled exactly as before, and the existing grammar-parity assertions pass with unchanged scope names
A theme that styles only comments colours every kind of comment, and styling line comments as well gives them their own style
An unknown style word is reported by validation and ignored when printing
Terminal output resets colour before every newline and, with codes removed, equals the plain output
HTML output uses only the documented class names, escapes text and has no inline styles; inline-styled HTML has styles and no classes
SVG output is a well-formed document with one text line per source line and a view box wide enough for the longest line
A stylesheet generated from any theme is valid CSS scoped to the container class, and changing only attributes changes only the attribute rule
A VS Code theme that colours properties orange colours attribute names orange
Colour chosen from a destination is terminal colour for a terminal and plain text for a file or when NO_COLOR is set

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: highlight/kind.go:133-175 maps each kind to the same TextMate scope the removed highlight/highlight.go constants held (BlockType storage.type.xcl, NameLabel entity.name.tag.xcl, Attribute variable.other.property.xcl, String string.quoted.double.xcl, Number constant.numeric.xcl, LineComment comment.line.double-slash.xcl, Inserted markup.inserted.diff, Error invalid.illegal.diagnostic, and so on for all 40 kinds). highlight/tokenize_test.go keeps the bracketed scope-string expectations (for example lines 359-382, [storage.type.xcl], [support.class.reference.xcl]) unchanged, and only the formatter they run through changed (markers at line 3361 uses token.Kind.Scope()). I did not run the tests; the verify summary reports them passing.

highlight/theme.go:1858-1871 Style falls back to the parent category when a kind has no style. highlight/terminal_test.go:137-146 TestThemeStylingOnlyCommentsColoursEveryKindOfComment expects Comment-only styling to colour // a, # b and /* c */ identically. highlight/terminal_test.go:148-155 TestThemeStylingLineCommentsGivesThemTheirOwnStyle expects LineComment 'bold green' to replace the Comment style for // only, while # and /* keep the Comment style. The whole-style replacement is tested in highlight/theme_test.go:TestThemeStyleReplacesTheParentStyleWhole.

highlight/theme.go Validate (around line 1878) returns an InvalidStyleError per unknown word via unknownWords (highlight/style.go:135-145). errors/highlight_errors.go:52-76 defines ErrInvalidStyle and InvalidStyleError. highlight/theme_test.go TestThemeValidateReportsAnUnknownWord and TestThemeValidateDetailsTheUnknownWord cover reporting. highlight/terminal_test.go TestTerminalWithAnUnknownStyleWordSucceeds and TestTerminalWithAnUnknownStyleWordAppliesTheKnownWords show printing ignores the word (highlight/style.go applyWord returns false and parsing never fails).

highlight/terminal.go:18-41 writes every styled token one line at a time, each non-empty line wrapped in SGR open and \x1b[0m close, with the newline written outside the codes, so a reset precedes every line break. Unstyled tokens carry no codes. Stripping codes gives the plain text since only codes are added. highlight/terminal_test.go:68-80 checks no newline falls inside a colour, including with Text styled. highlight/terminal_test.go:51-58 checks StripANSI(terminal) equals Plain output. Tests were not run by me.

highlight/html.go:16-34 HTML writes <pre class="xcl"> and spans with classes from classesOf (kind.Class, kebab-case), never a style attribute. Text is written without a span. escapeHTML (html.go:118-129) escapes & < > " '. highlight/html_test.go:157-168 checks only documented class names, :140-146 checks no 'style=' in HTML output, and :121-131 checks escaping. HTMLInline (html.go:41-63) writes style attributes and no class; html_test.go:188-192 checks no 'class=' in the output and :182-186 checks style is present.

highlight/svg.go:26-76 writes a standalone <svg xmlns=...> document with one <text xml:space="preserve"> per line (svgLines, svg.go:81-102, drops the trailing empty line). The viewBox width is 2*svgMargin + svgCharWidth*columns, where columns counts runes per line (svg.go:28-40), so it fits the longest line, and height fits every line. Escaping is via escapeHTML. highlight/svg_test.go:60-64 checks the output parses as XML, :84-103 checks one text element per line, :105-128 checks the viewBox, and :122-128 checks characters rather than bytes.

highlight/css.go:16-44 WriteCSS emits '.xcl { ... }' for Text and '.xcl .xcl-<kind> { ... }' for each kind the theme styles, in orderedKinds order, with resets (cssResets, css.go:48-71). Named colours are written as hex and dim as opacity. highlight/css_test.go:89-103 checks the stylesheet parses as plain CSS (braces, selector, ;-terminated declarations) and that every selector is scoped to .xcl. highlight/css_test.go:105-112 covers a loaded VS Code theme. highlight/css_test.go:149-163 TestWriteCSSChangingOnlyAttributesChangesOnlyTheAttributeRule checks that changing only Attribute changes only the attribute rule line.

highlight/vscode.go:130-149 LoadVSCodeTheme maps each kind's Scope() through the tokenColors rules, so a variable.other.property rule reaches Attribute, whose scope is variable.other.property.xcl (kind.go:141). highlight/vscode_test.go:115-123 TestLoadVSCodeThemeColoursPropertiesAsAttributes expects loaded[Attribute] to be #ff8800. highlight/vscode_test.go:125-135 checks the terminal output is \x1b[38;2;255;136;0ma\x1b[0m. Orange is taken to be #ff8800, which is what the test uses.

highlight/for.go:16-32 For returns Plain for a non-*os.File, a nil file, or a file that is not a character device (regular file), returns Plain when NO_COLOR is non-empty, and returns Terminal otherwise. highlight/for_test.go:69-113 covers a buffer, a regular file, a nil file, a closed file, a character device (Terminal), and a character device with NO_COLOR=1 (Plain).
